reason: Verified by driving master.html?v=approach&state=owner-empty. The dead end is real: act() in render-b.js:134 builds a plain type=button with no handler, so pressing Set the day with an empty field changes nothing measurable (body HTML length identical before and after, no aria-invalid, no [role=status] text, focus stays on the button). b.css contains no :invalid, no error, no hint and no disabled treatment anywhere in 633 lines, so the direction has no drawn failure path at all for its only form. The Preview sub-claim is also true: render-b.js:187 renders bar() with act('Preview') as the only action on a project with nothing in it. The seat is however factually wrong on the sentence it leans hardest on. The placeholder is not the grey the surface uses for real values: measured, the input value colour is rgb(255,255,255) and the placeholder computes to rgb(117,117,117) in every room, dimmer than the 62% secondary text (~rgb(165) in ink). In the ink room the frames were shot in, it does not read as an entered value. The sharper fact underneath is that rgb(117,117,117) is the Chromium UA default: no ::placeholder rule exists in b.css, shell.css, a.css or c.css, so the one grey the seat is arguing about was never declared, and in the paper room (which print forces) it lands at rgb(117) against a declared secondary of rgb(107), near enough to be indistinguishable. Confirming the finding, refuting its stated cause, and rejecting its fix.
sharpenedFix: Do NOT use input[type=date]: the native control drags in unstylable UA chrome (calendar indicator glyph, locale-ordered numeric segments, the browser picker panel) that cannot be held to Geist-only at two weights and three colours, and it abandons the human '3 October 2026' register the rest of the direction writes dates in. Keep the text field and the placeholder as the worked example. Instead, in b.css declare the placeholder explicitly rather than inheriting the UA grey, at a density clearly below the surface's own 62% secondary in BOTH grounds (.b-input::placeholder { color: var(--fore-38) } or similar, and verify the paper room, since print forces paper and today's UA grey is indistinguishable from real secondary ink there). Then draw the missing state rather than build app plumbing: add an invalid treatment to b.css (hairline at full ink density plus one sentence in the existing micro register, no new hue, status by ink density per the lock) and wire the one button locally the same way render-b.js:248 already wires the nudge steppers - on empty submit, preventDefault, keep focus in the field, set aria-invalid=true and aria-describedby to a [role=status] line reading 'Pick the date of the day first.' Do not write to the fixture and do not transition the deck to owner-flight; this is an eleven-state design deck, not a click-through prototype, and no other action in it navigates. Separately, drop Preview from the bar in the owner-empty branch of render-b.js:187 rather than disabling it, since a title tooltip is not reachable by keyboard or touch and an aria-disabled control the owner cannot use is worse than an absent one.
